# Protocol conformance fixtures

android-vectors.json is copied byte-for-byte from the MeshLive cross-platform conformance fixtures (the same file the Apple implementation's core tests use). It supplies Android-compatibility examples; it is not described here as a directly executed Android test run. Android PROTOCOL.md and Android source remain the wire authority.

GPL-3.0-or-later. SHA256 0c09640039f0a46af467aaee51729adbdc2c3f9b667e5b47cbb1e7d1f11c7359. Fixed private scalars are public test data and must never become production identities. Current native tests check all 18 BMS1 records/combined stream, 13 BME1 ciphertexts, handshake framing, all four BMH2 hellos/signatures, both identity fingerprints and both-role link/endpoint ECDH/HKDF directional keys. They do not yet test named identity persistence or all other fixture sections. BMH3 and discovery coverage is described below. No fixture values were edited or regenerated to make tests pass.

The CNG HKDF unit test additionally reproduces RFC 5869 Appendix A cases 1 and 3: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5869.html#appendix-A. No RFC implementation code is copied; the OS performs HKDF.

BMH3: bmh3-vectors.json is copied unchanged from the conformance fixtures; SHA256 01c6dfb65ae5324d94dd76effb7ef435157ee042faf24dcc32dfde88bea8b024. Android tools/bmh3_reference.py generated it (generator SHA256 6c2d1f919d8fc9ee7d356d9e4ebf484f52a87bc6754a009963ae7ceba2d83a54). scripts/check_bmh3_fixture.py separately confirms all five scenario names, 16 messages, 180 trace values and ten first records against the actual Android Kotlin fixture without running/building Android. Rust foundation tests reproduce the key schedule, AEAD blocks/messages, signatures, finished MACs and traffic keys; consuming disclosure states now also reproduce all message bytes. Application discovery/contact/lease/QR-policy integration is pending. JSON negative entries are descriptive, not executable cases, and include one intentionally accepted key-reuse counterexample. Reveal vectors (both records, signing inputs, callee record hash, node IDs) and negatives 1, 2c, 3, 4, 5, 7, 7b, 19-23, 26 and 27 are executable Rust tests; 13 remains the documented reuse counterexample.

## Discovery coverage

Native discovery tests round-trip the unchanged fixture's three manufacturer announcements and reproduce the six compact examples from Android's CompactDiscoveryAnnouncementTest/PROTOCOL (four base examples, call relay consent and audio-only), plus the rotating compact example. These test wire parsing/encoding and reserved/version gates only; src/rotating.rs separately reproduces the PROTOCOL rotating-ID salt/RDI, BDO1/BDX1 OPENING and contact/QR tag-key vectors and the opening check; no presence recognition, radio discovery or QR exchange is claimed.

Media framing tests reproduce the frozen BTV3 header and all six inner media packets byte for byte, including BTA1/BTA2, Opus config and rotation. Generic video-stream Opus examples need not satisfy the stricter experimental audio-only profile. Malformed bounds/flags/gaps, integer overflow, integrity tampering and nested Codec2 configuration extraction have focused native tests. Decoder output, source admission and playback remain separate work.

audio-live-vectors.json is copied unchanged from the conformance fixtures (SHA256 0f25c09955a725a43fd7104c951da717c657677489b008992b83c8d8a57287fb). It is an independent Python cryptography fixture using Android domains/formats, not a published Android signature vector. Native tests verify its certificate, both signed records and exact signing inputs. The three fixed preset headers match AudioLiveProtocolTest/PROTOCOL. Public fixed private scalars are used only in cfg(test) for focused signed-malformation, replay, budgets, duration and clock tests; production code cannot import these keys.

Mesh/watch tests also reproduce the unchanged BFG1 grant and all four frozen encrypted mesh envelopes (header, audio, video keyframe, End). Forwarding changes only TTL, preserving sealed endpoint bytes. Native admitted-reader tests enforce full source, stream, mesh order, TTL, mapped flags, marker/header agreement, repeated inner flags and a single header. The independent audio fixture is wrapped in fresh fixture BME1/BMS1 to test verified cap changes across coalesced input, before body consumption. Synthetic counter hand-over checks do not claim an application admission pass.

The independent signed-audio fixture also traverses fake GATT (20/244/512 byte values), BMS1/BMV1/BME1, the certificate/record guard and native libopus to produce one 960-sample silent PCM frame. Altering the signed body before otherwise-valid hop/endpoint sealing produces no PCM. Separate libopus tests decode silence with pre-skip and encode/decode generated non-private tone; they are not the complete upstream Opus conformance-vector suite, sound-output or acoustic-quality tests.

## HEVC and H.264 access units (Design HC)

hc/ holds the first 16 access units (two IDRs each) of four MeshLive Android hc-vectors captures from phone hardware encoders, encoding the generated raw test input (no camera, no private content) at 352x288, 15 FPS, 100 kbps: s24-hevc (Samsung S24, c2.exynos.hevc.encoder), asus-hevc (ASUS, OMX.qcom.video.encoder.hevc), m31-hevc (Samsung M31, OMX.Exynos.HEVC.Encoder) and a15s-h264 (OPPO A15s, OMX.MTK.VIDEO.ENCODER.AVC). Each file is byte-for-byte the Android packetiser's output (sets prepended to every IDR, 4-byte start codes); each directory's manifest.json keeps the capture's identity and every file's SHA-256, which the tests check before use. src/video/annexb/tests.rs runs them through the access-unit gate and the sender packetiser; src/video/hc_tests.rs decodes them with this PC's Media Foundation decoders. a15s-h264/au-000.bin and s24-hevc/au-000.bin are also embedded in the app as the decode start check's keyframes.
